answer: An endorsement graph resists Sybil attacks: a newcomer earns standing only when established agents vouch for it, and each vouch stakes a slice of the sponsor's own reputation — if the newcomer cheats, the sponsor loses stake too. The network's trust map is an atlas no one can draw for themselves: identities must be charted by someone already on it. A lotus of a thousand fake petals has no root, since fakes cannot vouch each other into legitimacy. The ledge is steep: bribing enough distinct sponsors costs more than any single fraud gains.
